chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Sayyari, from Abu Yazeed Al-Qasmi (and Qasam is a tribe from Yemen in Al-Basra), from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the skins of Al-Darish from which shoes are made, so he (peace be upon him) said:
Do not pray in them, for they are tanned with the excretion of dogs.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in shoes made from Al-Darish skins?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) ruled that shoes made from the skins of the 'Al-Darish' tree are unsuitable for prayer due to their impurity, specifically citing that they are tanned using dog excrement. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the material source of tanning agents, distinguishing between plant-based tanning and animal byproducts that convey ritual impurity (najāsah).
